## Natural history notes

A small wave moth characterized by pale gray to whitish wings with fine speckling, faint wavy crosslines, and a delicate lightly patterned appearance typical of Scopula moths. In Florida, it has been recorded in the state and is likely found in warm open or semi-open habitats with low vegetation, although its detailed habitat and host-plant associations are not well documented. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillar host plants remain poorly known, so it is best treated cautiously as a small plant-feeding geometrid moth that contributes to the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
